what.text: Firstmate takes an item from a backlog and gives it to a worker, which does the work in its own isolated worktree, a separate working copy of the project.
An agent decides what to dispatch and how to recover a stuck worker, while scripts enforce the gates: what may be dispatched, when a report is accepted, and when a worktree may be returned.
The captain approves each merge unless the yolo setting is on.

walkthrough.text: The item waits in the backlog as Queued. A spawn is accepted only for an unheld, unblocked item.
Spawning moves the item to In flight and creates an isolated worktree for the worker. If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued.
When the worker reports a PR or ready branch, the report is refused while the work exists only in the worker's disposable copy.
The task then waits for the merge authority, which is the captain unless yolo is on.
Teardown returns the worktree only if it is clean and the committed work has landed, and it removes the task record and closes the backlog item as one step.
If the backlog close fails, the pending-close record is kept and the next session start retries it.

glossary.definition: A stage a piece of work can be in. The states are listed first, under States of a piece of work.
A move from one state to another, shown as a card with its trigger and guard.
What starts a transition, and whether the agent or code decides that it has happened.
The condition that must hold for a transition to go ahead, and whether the agent or code checks it.
A number that some transitions change and others read, listed under Counters.
One sentence about firstmate, with its sources. Each claim has an id such as c1; the bracketed ids on this page link to the claims listed at the end.
The single firstmate commit the study read, shown at the top and in the footer. Nothing here describes any other version.
The label on a claim that says how the study came to it, shown beside the claim at the end.
A unit of work in a home's backlog. Dispatch refuses an item the home does not have.
The part of firstmate that judges what to do, such as which harness to use or whether to recover a worker. Scripts check the shape of its choices.
An agent that carries out one task in its own worktree.
A separate working copy of the project, isolated from the primary checkout, in which a worker does its task.
The kind of agent chosen for a dispatch. The agent picks it; scripts validate it.
The script that dispatches a task: it moves the item to In flight and refuses when it cannot.
An optional limit on the places a project has for workers. When all places are held, a spawn is deferred.
A kind of task, named next to scouts, whose finished work must be landed before its worktree is returned.
The one who approves merges and local-only landings when yolo is off.
A setting that, when off, makes the captain approve every merge.
The script that ends a task: it refuses a dirty worktree and removes the task record together with the backlog close.
A record kept when a backlog close fails, so a later session start can replay the close.
A wake after which the agent inspects a worker that may have stopped, looped or gone quiet.
Replacing a running agent with a new one in the same worktree.
